# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: all three wire positions, the display, and the light are unknown. I need the Mute to read the manual and tell me the required procedure. The Deaf can see the bomb’s markings, but I cannot hear them, so I will signal them to report their visual findings to the Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me the exact rule for choosing a wire. Also obtain the Deaf's complete visual description and relay it to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, yellow light, and wires in positions 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute should relay the manual instructions to you.

The Deaf reports: display 0, yellow light, and wire colors 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I must not cut yet. I will ask the Mute to provide the instruction needed to map these observations to a wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the bomb description: display 0, yellow light; positions 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Please send the manual's exact required cut position now.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0, light blue, wires unchanged: position 1 blue, position 2 red, position 3 green. Await Mute's manual-based instruction.

The latest visual report conflicts with the previous one: the light is now reported as blue rather than yellow. The wire colors and display remain known, but without the manual’s rule I cannot safely choose a wire. I will request the manual instruction and clarification of the light reading.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual's exact cut rule. Also, Deaf first reported a yellow light and now reports blue; please verify which light state the manual requires.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0, light white, wires unchanged: position 1 blue, position 2 red, position 3 green. I cannot interpret Mute's gestures; follow Mute's manual-based instruction.

The Deaf’s reports of the light have changed from yellow to blue to white, so I cannot rely on the light history without the manual’s interpretation. The stable tactile-relevant information relayed so far is display 0 and wire colors: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. I still have no manual instruction, so cutting would be unsafe. I will ask Mute directly for the exact position, not a gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state in words the exact wire position to cut, based on the manual and the current bomb information. Do not use gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb state: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute's latest gestures were thumbs down, love-you hand, then hand with fingers spread. Earlier sequences were also relayed; use the established manual/code meaning.

The latest report gives display 0, red light, and wire colors 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. The three gestures are not a reliable instruction to me: I cannot see them, and their meaning has not been stated in words. I will not guess a wire position. Mute must send the required position as spoken words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely decode the gesture sequence. State plainly: cut position 1, 2, or 3. Use words only.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light purple, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute's latest signal was one love-you hand gesture, the hand sign with thumb, index finger, and little finger extended.

The Deaf reports a current purple light, but I still have no spoken manual instruction from Mute. A gesture relayed by Deaf is not readable by me, and I cannot safely infer a wire position from it. I will continue waiting for Mute to state the position plainly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer in spoken words with exactly one of: cut position 1, cut position 2, or cut position 3. I cannot use the gesture report.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute's latest signal was thumbs down, then upward-pointing index finger three times.

Mute cannot speak, so the earlier requests for a spoken position were impossible. The relayed gestures are not yet an unambiguous wire instruction: thumbs-down followed by three index-up signs could encode a rule or a value, and guessing would detonate the bomb. I will establish a simple encoding: Mute should send Deaf exactly one, two, or three upward-index gestures, corresponding to the wire position; Deaf can then report the count in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal Deaf with only the upward-index gesture: one time for position 1, two times for position 2, or three times for position 3. No other gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signalled one love-you hand gesture: thumb, index finger, and little finger extended.

Mute’s latest love-you gesture is still not a known wire-position instruction. Since Mute can read the manual but cannot speak, I will establish a clear one-gesture code and have Deaf report which gesture Mute sends: thumbs up means position 1, thumbs down means position 2, and OK means position 3. I will not cut until Deaf relays one of those unambiguous choices.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use exactly one gesture to state the required wire: thumbs up means position 1, thumbs down means position 2, OK means position 3. Send no other gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light white, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signalled an upward-pointing index finger three times.

Mute sent the upward-index gesture three times, matching the counting code I established: three signals mean wire position 3. The Deaf again confirms the bomb’s visible state, but the manual-derived instruction is the decisive information. I will cut position 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
